I don't agree that Frigg and Freyja are the same. First, I'll give a few reasons why they're different and then I'll address the arguments for them being the same and why I find them lacking.

  1. They're from different tribes. Frigg is Aesir. Freyja is Vanir. Freyja, her brother, and father came over to Asgard as hostages after the Aesir-Vanir war.

  2. They have different fathers. Frigg is daughter of Fjörgynn (associated with earth) Freyja is daughter of Njordr (associated with the sea).

  3. They have different siblings There is no mention of Frigg having any siblings. Freyja is the twin-sister of Frey.

  4. They have different children. Frigg has two sons, Balder and Hodr and step-children. Freyja has two daughters, Hnoss and Gersemi.

  5. They have different halls Frigg hangs out in Fensalir a watery boggy place. Freyja hangs out in Folkvangr a grassy meadow, where her hall Sessrumnir is.

  6. They are both mentioned as separate goddesses in the sagas. For example in Lokasenna, Loki insults both Frigg and Freyja separately. They are treated as two different people. Elsewhere, Frigg is named as the highest among the goddesses with Freyja being second.

Re: Similar Names

Frigg and Freyja sound alike, but Frigg is a name, likely meaning Beloved, where as Freyja is a title. Frey and Freya are titles--Lord and Lady, respectively.

Re: Husbands with similar names.

Odin and Odr do sound similar--so what? There are Dvergr with names that sound similar to Odin and Odr too, for example, Oinn and Otr.

Is it really that strange to think more than one deity could be associated with some aspect of the mind, soul, spirit, madness, poetry, song, frenzy, faith, prophecy, etc? The root word has a lot of meanings. I'd be surprised if there weren't a lot of forgotten minor deities that shared the root as well.

Other than the name, the only thing the two have in common is they go on journeys (but so do Thor and Loki and others). There are some who believe that Odr and Freyja's story (which is a latter addition) is actually a retelling of Adonis and Aphrodite. With Odr being a translation of Adon--to sing. Adonis, like Odr, is always leaving Aphrodite to go hunt, just as Freyja is left by Odr, and in the end both Aphrodite and Freyja cry for their loves.

Not saying I agree that Odr is Adonis, but I don't agree he's Odin either. He's not treated as though he is Odin and Freyja does not behave like the mother of Balder and Hodr. And their names sounding alike isn't strong enough link to dismiss these things--especially with such a common root.

Re: Pantheon Role

They don't have a similar Pantheon role. Frigg is a Wisdom Goddess associated with forethought, and marriage.. Freya is a goddess similar to the Sumerian Inanna representing Love, Lust, Beauty and War.

On the surface both have an association with love, but Frigg's is an enduring deep love such as between husband and wife, mother and child; whereas Freya's is more a passionate lustful love between lovers just as the goddess such as Inanna and Aphrodite represent. Also one could argue they maybe both share association with magic--but all women in Northern culture were associated with magic. That's not particularly special.
